group: one-number map (3n minus a power of two), cryptid
title: What is known about 1RB1RE_1LC0RA_1RD0LB_1LB1RC_1LF0RD_---0LE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RE_1LC0RA_1RD0LB_1LB1RC_1LF0RD_---0LE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and reduced to a map on one number. Lean proves (kernel, no native_decide) that the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of 1 under the map next reaches none. In closed form the map is n → 3n − 2ci + i + 3 for ci < n < ci+1, with ci = 10·2i − i − 7, and it halts exactly when n = ci+1. Iterated 1,250,000 times, the orbit never lands on a threshold; n then has about 833,000 binary digits. A probability argument says a hit is ever less likely (about 1/2i per step), so the machine is expected never to halt, but no proof is known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 36,587 cells have been visited and 18,743 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.066). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.523).

claims.title: The rules of a round
claims.text: Every rule of both phases, for all values of the counts: the sample S (n+3) becomes V (n+2) 0 0, one bounce V (K+1) i (m+1) → V K (i+1) m, the end of a sub-phase V (K+4) i 0 → V K 0 (2i+5), the five ways the first phase ends (one of them the halt), and the second phase T x z → S (2x+z+4).

claims.title: The map
claims.text: For all K, i, m: V K i m reaches the sample S n when ph K i m = some n, and halts when ph K i m = none; ph is a recursive function following the rules one bounce at a time.

claims.title: Halts if and only if the orbit hits none
claims.text: From blank tape the machine reaches S 1 in 4 steps; so it halts if and only if the orbit of 1 under next n = ph (n−1) 0 0 reaches none.

claims.title: The closed form of the map
claims.text: next(n) = 3n − 2c<sub>i</sub> + i + 3 for c<sub>i</sub> < n < c<sub>i+1</sub> and a halt for n = c<sub>i+1</sub>, with c<sub>i</sub> = 10·2<sup>i</sup> − i − 7. Derived by adding up the sub-phases (the right block runs through 5·2<sup>t</sup> − 5 pairs) and checked against Lean's definition for all n < 10,000; not proved in Lean.

claims.title: The map matches the machine
claims.text: The 19 samples S n of the first 10<sup>9</sup> machine steps are exactly the first 19 points of the orbit of 1: 1, 7, 18, 34, 45, 78, 100, 166, ...

claims.title: No halt in 1,250,000 map steps
claims.text: Iterating the closed form with Python big integers, the orbit of 1 never lands on a threshold in 1,250,000 steps; n then has about 833,000 bits, so the machine has run far more than 2<sup>800000</sup> steps.

claims.title: Why a halt looks unlikely
claims.text: Write n = c<sub>i</sub> + d; the offset d, between 0 and 10·2<sup>i</sup>, becomes 3d + i + 3, wrapping into the next level or the one after. A halt needs the offset to land exactly on the end of its level; treating d as random the chance is about 1/(10·2<sup>i</sup>) per step, and i grows by about 0.67 per step, so the expected number of future hits is far below 2<sup>-100000</sup>. A halt at the next step needs 3n = 4c<sub>i</sub> + 3, possible only for i ≡ 0, 1 (mod 6); the closest approach seen was |3n − 4c<sub>i</sub> − 3|/c<sub>i</sub> ≈ 5.9·10<sup>-6</sup>.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It is equivalent (in Lean) to whether the orbit of 1 under the map ever lands exactly on a threshold c<sub>i</sub>; that is a Collatz-like question with no known method of attack.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows, but the question is now about one number. Read at the moments the head is at the left end, the tape holds a single number n; Lean proves that the machine halts exactly when a simple map on n, started at 1, lands on one of the thresholds 3, 12, 31, 70, 149, ... The map has been iterated 1.25 million times without that happening.

facts.text: Lean: the machine halts iff the orbit of 1 lands on a threshold.
No hit; n has about 833,000 bits by then.
Chance of a hit at a step of level i; i grows at every few steps.

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: One number, and a ruler
html: Whenever the head is at the left end of the tape, the tape reads
S n  =  C>0 (10)^n 1
a block of n pairs 10. From blank tape the first such sample is S 1, after 4 steps. A round has two phases.
Phase 1 turns the block into a run of 2n − 2 ones and then measures it: the tape becomes

and each bounce takes two ones from the left and one pair from the right block and adds two pairs to the middle: V (K+1) i (m+1) → V K (i+1) m. When the right block is used up, the middle block moves over to the right with five extra pairs: V (K+4) i 0 → V K 0 (2i+5). So the right block is a ruler of 0, 5, 15, 35, 75, ... = 5·2t − 5 pairs, doubling each time, paid for by the ones on the left.

The phase ends when the ones run out. Most of the time this happens in the middle of a bounce sequence (V 0 i (m+1)); at the end of a sub-phase it can end four ways, V 2K i 0 for K = 0, 1, 2, 3, and K = 2 is the halting transition (state F reading 0).
Phase 2 turns C>0 (10)^x 111 0 (10)^z 1 back into a sample, S (2x + z + 4).

sections.heading: Triple, and subtract a power of two
html: With thresholds ci = 10·2i − i − 7 (−1, 3, 12, 31, 70, 149, 308, 627, ...), for ci < n ≤ ci+1:

next(n) = 3n − 2c_i + i + 3     if n < c_(i+1)
          HALT                  if n = c_(i+1)

Lean defines the map one bounce at a time and proves the machine follows it; the closed form above is checked against that definition for every n below 10,000. The orbit of 1, which matches the machine's samples exactly:

The left end of the tape moves once per round while n roughly triples, so the left side grows like the logarithm of time; the head sweeps the whole block, so the right side grows like its square root.

sections.heading: Only by landing exactly on a threshold
html: Write n = ci + d. The offset d, somewhere between 0 and 10·2i, becomes 3d + i + 3: it triples and wraps into the next level or the one after. The machine halts only if the offset lands exactly on the end of a level. In 1,250,000 steps of the map that never happened; n has 833,000 bits by then.

If the offset behaves like a random number, the chance of an exact hit at a step of level i is about 1/(10·2i), and these chances add up to almost nothing: the machine is expected to run forever. Proving it would mean controlling the digits of an orbit of a map like n → 3n − 2k, a Collatz-like problem, so this machine is a cryptid.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.066). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.523).
After 109 steps the tape spans 36,587 cells (54 left of the start, 33,791 right), with a density of 1s of 0.512.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A one-number map n → 3n − 2c_i + i + 3 between thresholds c_i = 10·2^i − i − 7; halts iff the orbit of 1 lands exactly on a threshold (reduction proved in Lean). Not hit in 1.25·10^6 map steps.
